prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a land the 1842 Wentworth letter says the gospel had reached (East Indies aside)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a land the 1842 Wentworth letter names as reached by the restored gospel (leave aside 'the East Indies')
prompts.citation: Church History, 1 March 1842 (Wentworth letter), Joseph Smith Papers, p. 709 and note 29
prompts.note: 'Palestine' in the letter covers both ISR and PSE. 'East Indies' is left out because the term is too vague to map to one country.
prompts.summary: In 1842 Joseph Smith sent Chicago editor John Wentworth a history of the Church that ends with the 13 Articles of Faith. It reports the gospel had spread across the United States and the British Isles, and that the standard of truth had been raised in Germany, Palestine, New Holland (Australia) and the East Indies.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: It names England, Scotland and Wales; the Twelve preached across the British Isles in 1840-41.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: The letter says the elders had planted the gospel in almost every state in the Union.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Germany is named; Orson Hyde passed through Munich on his way to Jerusalem.

answers.name: Ireland
answers.fact: Ireland is named in the letter; the island is shared today by Ireland and the United Kingdom.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Palestine is named; Orson Hyde dedicated the land at Jerusalem on 24 October 1841.

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Palestine in 1842 also covered today's West Bank.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: New Holland is named; English convert William James Barratt emigrated there in July 1840.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where Jesus or a disciple cast out an evil spirit (not the Gadarene swine or the boy after the Transfiguration)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a town or region where Jesus or one of his disciples, being there, cast out an evil spirit (not the Gadarene swine or the boy healed after the Transfiguration)
prompts.note: Jordan and Syria do not count: the Gadarene site is disputed. Samaria is in the West Bank (Palestine).
prompts.summary: Jesus showed power over evil spirits from his first sermon at Capernaum, and he healed a Gentile girl near Tyre and Sidon. His servants carried the same power: Philip in Samaria, Paul at Philippi, where he freed a slave girl from a spirit of divination, and at Ephesus, where even cloths from him healed.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: In the synagogue at Capernaum Jesus rebuked an unclean spirit, and cast out devils throughout Galilee (Mark 1:21-26, 39).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: At Philippi Paul commanded the spirit of divination to come out of a damsel (Acts 16:16-18).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: In the borders of Tyre and Sidon Jesus cast the devil out of a Syrophenician woman's daughter (Mark 7:24-30).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Philip, one of the seven, preached in the city of Samaria, and unclean spirits came out of many (Acts 6:5; 8:5-7).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: At Ephesus evil spirits went out of the sick through handkerchiefs from Paul (Acts 19:11-12).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place in Assyria's conquest and resettlement of Israel, 2 Kings 15-17 (leave out Ijon)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place named in Assyria's conquest and resettlement of the northern kingdom in 2 Kings 15-17: towns Tiglath-pileser took, Samaria, the lands the captives were sent to, and the cities settlers came from (sites agreed by scholars only)
prompts.note: Samaria is in the West Bank (Palestine); Hazor, Kedesh and Galilee are in Israel.
prompts.summary: Tiglath-pileser of Assyria took Gilead, Galilee, Kedesh and Hazor, then Damascus. Shalmaneser besieged Samaria, and in 721 BC its people were carried to Assyria, the Habor by the river of Gozan and the cities of the Medes, while settlers from Babylon, Cuthah and Hamath took their place (2 Kgs 15-17).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Israel was carried away into Assyria, and settlers came from Babylon and Cuthah (2 Kgs 17:6, 24).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Tiglath-pileser took Abel-beth-maachah, Kedesh and Hazor, and Galilee (2 Kgs 15:29).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Shalmaneser besieged Samaria three years before it fell (2 Kgs 17:5-6).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Assyria took Damascus (2 Kgs 16:9), and settlers were brought from Hamath (2 Kgs 17:24).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Captives from Samaria were placed in the cities of the Medes (2 Kgs 17:6).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Tiglath-pileser took Gilead and carried its people captive (2 Kgs 15:29).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a city or people in Nehemiah 1-4 and 13, from Shushan to Tobiah the Ammonite (leave out the Arabians)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a city or people named in Nehemiah 1-4 and 13 (leaving out the Arabians, whose land is unclear): the Persian palace at Shushan, Jerusalem's builders from Jericho and Tekoa, the wall's opponents (Samaria's army, Tobiah the Ammonite, the Ashdodites), and the men of Tyre who sold fish
prompts.note: Jericho, Tekoa and Samaria are in the West Bank (Palestine); Ashdod is in Israel. Jerusalem is scored as Israel.
prompts.summary: Nehemiah, cupbearer to the Persian king at Shushan, won leave to rebuild Jerusalem's wall. Builders came from towns such as Jericho and Tekoa, while Sanballat, Tobiah the Ammonite, Geshem the Arabian and the Ashdodites mocked and plotted. The wall was finished in fifty and two days (Neh 1-6).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Nehemiah was cupbearer to Artaxerxes in Shushan the palace (Neh 1:1, 11).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: He rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem; the Ashdodites joined the plot against it (Neh 2:17; 4:7).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Tobiah the Ammonite mocked the builders, and no Ammonite or Moabite was to enter the congregation (Neh 2:19; 13:1).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Men of Jericho and the Tekoites built sections of the wall, and Sanballat spoke before the army of Samaria (Neh 3:2, 5; 4:2).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Men of Tyre sold fish and wares in Jerusalem on the sabbath (Neh 13:16).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Nehemiah went to Artaxerxes king of Babylon before returning (Neh 13:6).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a city or town named in Acts 18, from Paul's stay in Corinth to Apollos at Ephesus
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a city or town named in Acts 18, the chapter of Paul's stay in Corinth and his return to Antioch
prompts.note: Only cities count, not regions, so Syria and North Macedonia do not. Antioch is in Turkey.
prompts.summary: Acts 18 covers Paul's long stay in Corinth, where he made tents with Aquila and Priscilla, Jews expelled from Rome. He sailed from Cenchrea to Ephesus, landed at Caesarea, and went down to Antioch. Meanwhile Apollos of Alexandria arrived at Ephesus and was taught the way of God more perfectly.

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Paul left Athens for Corinth, stayed a year and a half, and shaved his head in Cenchrea (Acts 18:1, 11, 18).

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Claudius had commanded all Jews to leave Rome, so Aquila and Priscilla came to Corinth (Acts 18:2).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Paul landed at Caesarea and went up to salute the church; he hoped to keep the feast at Jerusalem (Acts 18:21-22).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Paul reasoned at Ephesus, then went down to Antioch, today's Antakya (Acts 18:19-22).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Apollos, mighty in the scriptures, was born at Alexandria (Acts 18:24).
